variants.candidate: With too little Earth, the ground under you is shallow, and every load goes straight through to your knees. Nothing stays put without a push from outside. Sleep and eat before you decide anything.
variants.original: Run thin, the ground doubts its own bearing: steadiness performed, footing borrowed. Your chart asks you to feed the self. Keep one promise to yourself so long it becomes terrain.

variants.candidate: With too little Wood, nothing grows through the ground to hold it, and soil without roots spreads wherever it is pushed. Take on one demand with a date on it.
variants.original: Run thin, nothing roots in you: ground with no claim on it, steadiness serving no living thing. Your chart asks for roots. Take on something growing and let it grip.

variants.candidate: You carry little Water. The ground has banks and no river between them, and plans stay drawn while fields go dry. Start one thing this month and let it run.
variants.original: Run thin, the banks hold no river: structure ready, nothing flowing, canals waiting on rain. Your chart asks you to court the current. Go where things move and channel some.

variants.candidate: With too little Fire, the ground goes cold under the seed, and the soil feeds on an old harvest. Take in one warm thing a week, a teacher or a book.
variants.original: Run thin, the field goes gray: duties held on cold ground, nothing warm coming in. Your chart asks you to feed the fire that feeds you. Accept warmth. Attend the feast.

variants.candidate: With too little Metal, the ground keeps every bit of its ore, all that weight and patience and nothing coming out with a finished shape. Say one thing plainly before it is perfect.
variants.original: Run thin, the ore stays buried: depth with no expression, patience that never mints anything. Your chart asks you to bring metal up. Finish a piece, publish the standard.
